panel_intro: Answer a few quick questions. The range updates as you go — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

distance_field.label: Distance to tow (miles)
distance_field.help: From the pickup spot to the shop, home, or safe drop-off.

state_field.label: State (optional)
state_field.help: Doesn't change the estimate below — used to point you to the right local rules and guides.

options.label: Not sure / prefer not to say

select_fields.label: Vehicle type
select_fields.help: Bigger or heavier vehicles need bigger equipment.

select_fields.label: When do you need the tow?
select_fields.help: Nights, weekends, and holidays usually cost more.

select_fields.label: What's the situation?
select_fields.help: Winching and accident recovery take more time and equipment.

options.label: Flatbed needed — AWD, low clearance, etc.

factor_explanations.distance: Distance is usually the single biggest factor after the base fee — most companies charge a flat hook-up fee plus a per-mile rate.
factor_explanations.vehicle: Bigger or heavier vehicles need bigger tow trucks and more time to secure safely.
factor_explanations.timing: Night, weekend, and holiday calls usually cost more since fewer drivers are on shift.
factor_explanations.situation: A car that rolls onto a flatbed in minutes costs less than one that's stuck and needs winching, or one involved in an accident.
factor_explanations.heavy_duty: Heavy-duty vehicles need specialized equipment most companies bill extra for.
factor_explanations.storage_days: Storage is billed separately from the tow itself, usually starting the same day or the next.

savings_tips: Check your auto insurance policy or roadside plan first — you may already have towing coverage.
If it's safe, wait for normal business hours instead of paying an after-hours surcharge.
If it's safe to choose, ask to go to a shop or address of your choice instead of a private impound lot — this can avoid storage fees entirely.
Compare two local companies if you have a minute — rates for the same job can vary more than people expect.
Ask if your membership (auto club, some credit cards, some insurers) already covers part of the cost.
common_mistakes: Authorizing storage without asking whether it can be avoided.
Accepting the first quoted price without asking for an itemized breakdown.
Not photographing the vehicle's condition before it's loaded.
Leaving valuables or personal items in the vehicle.
Not confirming exactly where the vehicle is being taken before the truck leaves.
Not asking whether mileage and after-hours fees are already included in the quote.
before_tow_checklist: Take photos of the vehicle from all sides before it's hooked up.
Remove valuables and anything you can safely grab.
Confirm exactly where the vehicle is going before the truck leaves.
Confirm the total price and payment method before the driver arrives.
Note the company name and driver name or ID, just in case.

phone_script.intro: Read this out loud while you're on the phone — it covers what actually matters.
lines: Hi, I have a {vehicle_label} that needs a tow.
Can you give me the total estimated price, including hookup, mileage, and any after-hours fees?
Will there be storage charges, and when do they start?
Where will my vehicle be taken?
About how long until the truck arrives?
